claim: NixOS's systemd.user.services creates REAL systemd user units started by the user's own systemd --user instance, but installs the unit for every user via /etc/systemd/user, unlike home-manager which installs per-user
stance_target: NixOS user services are a genuine per-user mechanism but with system-wide unit installation semantics that must be accounted for in fleet deployment
quoted_support: NixOS's systemd.user.services in NixOS creates REAL systemd user units (started by the user's own systemd --user instance) but installs the unit file for EVERY user via /etc/systemd/user (vs home-manager which installs per-user).

claim: NixOS-installed systemd user services do NOT start/restart on 'nixos-rebuild switch' the way system services do; the user must relog so the user instance restarts, or the operator must handle it manually
stance_target: user services as a fleet-deployment mechanism on NixOS (they have a rebuild/restart gap that system services lack)
scope_conditions: NixOS; systemd user services deployed via systemd.user.services
quoted_support: NixOS-installed systemd user services do NOT start/restart on 'nixos-rebuild switch' like system services do — you must relog so the user instance restarts from scratch, or handle it manually.

claim: For a single user's service, home-manager is the recommended mechanism in NixOS; the alternative pattern is a system service with serviceConfig.User
stance_target: a fleet agent targeting every host should run as a system service (optionally with User= scoping) rather than per-user installs
quoted_support: for a single user's service, home-manager is the recommended mechanism; (3) alternative pattern is a system service with serviceConfig.User.
